results.failure: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/browser.rs:1781; serialized requestBodyPreviewKind actual text, expected binary

fixture_bytes.interpretation: The prefixes resemble TLS record framing. Every byte is below 0x80, so Rust accepts the sequence as UTF-8 even though it begins with control characters and is not human-readable text.

frozen_behavior.message: browser.network.requests is not supported on WKWebView

sources: CLI/cmux.swift:14689-14692 at the frozen canonical commit

canonical_comparison.parity_interpretation: Windows proxy-stream capture is a platform-equivalent extension beyond the frozen WKWebView implementation. Canonical cmux therefore neither requires nor supports labeling opaque bytes as text. The Windows result must be judged by the advertised proxy observer semantics and internal wire consistency.

reasons: A successful CONNECT establishes a byte tunnel; bytes after the broker handshake are not an HTTP entity body and have no origin MIME metadata at this observation layer.

For HTTPS, captured prefixes are encrypted TLS records. Treating UTF-8 decodability as proof of text leaks control characters into a field advertised as a text preview and misrepresents opaque ciphertext.

The record itself declares source proxy-stream-tunnel, method CONNECT, empty headers, and a note that encrypted origin headers remain unavailable without interception; binary is the only classification consistent with those fields.
The same BrowserNetworkRecord is returned directly and serialized to camelCase JSON. Classification must not differ between browser, session bridge, and control-socket clients.

non_empty_prefix.size: N, the captured prefix length supplied to the recorder
non_empty_prefix.truncated: true when N exceeds the body preview limit or the proxy observation says more bytes existed; otherwise false

empty_prefix.truncated: the proxy observation's truncation flag; an empty captured prefix can still represent omitted bytes

opaque_connect_tunnel.headers: requestHeaders and responseHeaders remain empty because origin headers are encrypted or otherwise opaque
opaque_connect_tunnel.status: responseStatus 200 means the proxy/broker tunnel handshake succeeded; it is not an origin HTTPS response status
opaque_connect_tunnel.mime_rule: Never infer text from MIME for an opaque tunnel. No origin Content-Type is observable without interception.
opaque_connect_tunnel.transport_rule: The rule applies equally to SOCKS5 and HTTP CONNECT because transport selection does not make post-handshake bytes textual.
opaque_connect_tunnel.url_rule: Port 443 uses https://host/; other ports use tcp://host:port/. The classification rule is based on the opaque-tunnel production path, not the URL scheme alone.

cleartext_http_and_custom_scheme.separation_rule: Do not force cleartext HTTP or Tauri custom-scheme bodies to binary; those paths carry entity bodies and may expose Content-Type.
content_type_precedence: An explicit binary media type is binary even when its bytes happen to be valid UTF-8.
Textual media types include text/*, application/json and *+json, application/xml and *+xml, application/javascript, application/x-www-form-urlencoded, and application/graphql.
A textual media type is previewable as text only when the captured bytes decode as UTF-8; unsupported or invalid charsets fall back to binary rather than lossy decoding.
With absent or ambiguous Content-Type, require valid UTF-8 and no disallowed control characters before labeling text.

utf8_control_heuristic.disallowed_controls: Other Unicode control characters, including NUL, C0 framing bytes, DEL, and C1 controls, make an untyped body binary.

cleartext_http_and_custom_scheme.audit_note: The current generic network_body_text helper ignores Content-Type and uses UTF-8 validity alone. That is an adjacent classifier weakness, but broadening the three-red fix to MIME policy would change established cleartext output without dedicated red coverage.

wire_serialization.consistency: In-memory browser replies, session-bridged observations, and control-socket JSON must expose identical preview classifications and truncation values. No session-specific reclassification or second serializer is permitted.

root_cause.primary: record_proxy_tunnel_observation_with_attribution calls network_body_text for upstream and downstream prefixes. network_body_text classifies every non-empty valid UTF-8 sequence as text and checks neither semantic source nor control characters.
root_cause.why_all_three_fail: The direct browser record test, JSON serializer test, and session bridge test all converge on the same browser tunnel recorder. Their three failures are one classifier defect, not three independent runtime defects.
root_cause.why_tls_fixture_is_text_today: 0x16, 0x03, 0x01/0x03, and the short length bytes are valid single-byte UTF-8 code points, despite being C0 controls.
